auth.notes: Tuya account + per-device pairing tokens; device-side auth is the device id / local key pair issued at pairing. Not needed for LAN control once the local key is known.

endpoints.name: Tuya OpenAPI / app API
endpoints.notes: No tuya*.com hostnames appear as plaintext anywhere in the Smart Life app (code, resources, or the network/security native libs) — region endpoints are delivered at runtime by Tuya's config service. The hosts listed are the publicly documented Tuya endpoint families, recorded for orientation; consumers should use the LAN protocol, not these.

cloud.failure_mode: Nothing breaks at runtime: with the local key extracted, full local control via tinytuya / localtuya / tuya-local keeps working with the device permanently WAN-blocked — UDP 6666/6667 and TCP 6668 are plain local sockets (no DNS redirect needed). Losing the Tuya cloud removes remote (out-of-home) access, the app panel UI, new-device pairing, OTA firmware delivery, and — the one sharp edge — local-key extraction for a not-yet-extracted unit. Tuya Inc. itself is alive (NYSE: TUYA, actively shipping as of 2026); the anonymous white-label OEMs behind individual clones come and go, which affects firmware support, not connectivity.
hosts: images.tuyaus.com — OTA firmware images (per-product, auth-gated URLs)
cloud.notes: The ONLY hard cloud dependency for stock-firmware local control is one-time local-key extraction: pair the device in Smart Life, link the app account to a free Tuya IoT developer project, and pull the device id + local key with the tinytuya wizard. Tuya has broken this flow for some account types in the past — verify current status before buying hardware for a local-only install. Nuclear option: the WB2S/CB2S (BK7231T/N) modules are UART-flashable (RX1/TX1 pads, 3.3 V) with LibreTiny/ESPHome or OpenBeken via ltchiptool — a complete ESPHome config mapping all 12 RQ400A DPs is published (see helpful_urls) — after which no Tuya account or key is involved at all. CloudCutter OTA-flashing works only on unpatched firmware batches; feasibility on shipped units is an open question.
cloud.vendor_service: Tuya cloud (Smart Life / Tuya Smart platform)

audible_alarm_off.description: Disable the buzzer (DP 12 = false). SAFETY: silences the primary local alert.

audible_alarm_on.description: Enable the buzzer (DP 12 = true). SAFETY: the buzzer is the primary local alert.

dp_query.description: Request current DP values (the state poll).

heartbeat.description: Keep-alive ping; the device answers with the same command.

muffle_alarm.description: Silence the currently active alarm once (DP 14 = true; auto-resets).

self_test.description: Trigger an MCU self-test (DP 9 = true); result appears in DP 1.

set_alarm_duration.description: Set how long the alarm sounds (DP 3, seconds).

duration.description: Alarm duration in seconds, 0-180 (the number entity's range).

set_alarm_melody.description: Pick the alarm melody (DP 8, enum). RQ400A: five melodies.

melody.description: Melody index as the STRING the enum DP carries on the wire — "0".."4", matching the select entity's option keys.

discovery.notes: Tuya LAN discovery is UDP broadcast on ports 6666 and 6667; each device emits/answers framed datagrams (0x000055aa header … 0x0000aa55 trailer) whose payload carries the device id, product key and protocol version (3.1/3.3/3.4). On 3.3/3.4 devices the discovery payload is AES-encrypted with a well-known SDK-embedded key documented in tinytuya/tuyapi rather than reproduced here. Confirmed present in the Smart Life app: constants 6666/6667/6668 and the broadcast-monitor service (6666/6667 discovery, 6668 TCP control).

identification.notes: No device-level FCC ID exists for these white-label goods; the Tuya modules inside are certified under grantee 2ANDL (Hangzhou Tuya Information Technology Co., Ltd.), e.g. 2ANDL-WB2S. MAC OUIs are not listed: they belong to the module and vary per clone, so they would rank noise rather than identify this family.

device.name: Tuya WiFi Combustible Gas Sensor (rqbj family)
device.notes:
A Tuya Wi-Fi gas alarm is a two-processor device: a Tuya Wi-Fi module (WB2S/CB2S — Beken BK7231T/N — on the documented units; WB3S/WBR3 on some clones) talks the Tuya LAN/cloud protocols, and a separate sensor MCU (RunJet RJM8L151F6P6 on the DY-RQ400A) owns the gas sensor element, buzzer and LEDs. The two are linked by a UART running the TuyaMCU serial protocol (9600 8N1 on the RQ400A); the Wi-Fi module is essentially a bridge that exposes the MCU's state as Tuya DPS datapoints. An important safety consequence: alarm detection, the fixed gas threshold and the local buzzer live in the MCU and work with no Wi-Fi at all — the Wi-Fi side only reports state and accepts configuration. Whether a given unit's MCU keeps working with the Wi-Fi module physically removed is an open question (not verified).
The "433MHz" in the marketing copy of these listings is NOT the control channel. It is a sub-1GHz receiver on the MCU board used to pair cheap RF remote controls (alarm silence / self-test) and, on some listings, wireless gas-shutoff valves. No app or cloud traffic uses it; all IP traffic is 2.4 GHz 802.11 b/g/n, plus module BLE used only for assisted pairing. Whether valve pairing state is visible in any DP is an open question — no DP for it is documented.
On the gas-detection behavior itself (DY-RQ400A, per the ESPHome device page): the trip threshold is fixed in MCU firmware at 7±3 %LEL CH4 and is NOT adjustable over Wi-Fi; once tripped, the alarm latches until the measured level falls below half the trip point. The Wi-Fi module can only read state and set configuration DPs (alarm duration, melody, audible on/off, muffle).
SAFETY: this is a life-safety sensor. Local control via this spec must never be treated as a substitute for the device's own standalone alarm function, and any automation should treat loss of connectivity as a fault worth surfacing, not silence.

openness.notes: tinytuya (and make-all/tuya-local for Home Assistant) are the authoritative, hardware-tested implementations; this spec documents the protocol rather than competing with them. The gas-sensor device UI in the vendor apps is a cloud-delivered React Native panel bundle — the Smart Life app contains no gas-sensor-specific code at all (zero hits for the category name or DP codes anywhere in it), so the DP model here rests on community sources corroborated by the app's generic Tuya LAN/DPS machinery, not on device-specific app code.

issued_to_client: local key (recoverable once via Tuya IoT developer account + tinytuya wizard)
credentials.notes: During EZ/AP provisioning the passphrase travels inside Tuya's pairing exchange rather than as cleartext on the open AP; post-setup, all LAN traffic is AES-128-ECB under the per-device local key, so the local key IS the credential — treat it as a password and LAN-segment the device.
stored_on_device: Tuya device id + 16-char local key (issued at pairing)

factory_reset.effect: Clears Wi-Fi credentials and the cloud binding (device id / local key pair is reissued on re-pairing), returning the unit to pairing mode. MCU-side alarm function and thresholds are unaffected — the MCU never depended on Wi-Fi.

procedures.indicator: LED enters fast-blink pairing mode (EZ); hold again for slow-blink AP mode.
procedures.name: Press and hold the pairing button (~5 seconds)

steps.action: With the sensor powered, press and hold its button for about 5 seconds until the LED blinks rapidly, then release.
steps.notes: Generic stock-Tuya-firmware behavior (same as every Tuya Wi-Fi gadget), not verified on this specific hardware; per-clone button placement and LED semantics vary.

methods.description: EZ mode: with the device in pairing mode (fast-blinking LED after holding the button), the app broadcasts the Wi-Fi credentials plus a cloud-issued pairing token via SmartLink broadcast/multicast (native libThingSmartLink / ThingSmartLink.smartLink in the SDK). Requires a Tuya cloud account in Smart Life or Tuya Smart.
methods.name: EZ mode: credentials broadcast over the air

steps.action: Hold the pairing button until the LED blinks fast — EZ mode.
Broadcast the Wi-Fi credentials plus a cloud-issued pairing token over SmartLink broadcast/multicast from the app.
The sensor joins the Wi-Fi network and registers with the Tuya cloud.
steps.expect: The LED stops blinking and the device appears in Smart Life / Tuya Smart.

methods.description: AP mode (device hotspot, slow-blinking LED — entered from EZ mode by holding the pairing button again on stock Tuya firmware): the device hosts an open AP (SmartLife-XXXX naming on most clones) and receives credentials over the same framed Tuya protocol on the setup network. Supported by the SDK; exact per-clone AP naming unverified.
methods.name: AP mode: the device's own hotspot

methods.description: BLE-assisted pairing: the WB2S/CB2S module's BLE radio advertises during pairing mode and the app hands credentials over GATT before the device joins Wi-Fi. SDK-supported; not exercised by this project.
methods.name: BLE-assisted pairing

setup.notes: Provisioning is the standard Tuya flow, confirmed as generic SDK capability in the Smart Life app (not replayed against this hardware by this project). After pairing, one further cloud-dependent step is needed for stock-firmware local control: extracting the per-device 16-char local key (see cloud.notes).

rejoin.notes: No documented in-place credential update; treat a router/SSID change as factory reset + re-pair. The old network does not need to be up.

testing.notes: No hardware has been exercised by this project. Every fact below is derived from clean-room static analysis of the Smart Life app (see `sources`) cross-checked against public community documentation (ESPHome device page for the DY-RQ400A, make-all/tuya-local issue #2434 and device configs, tinytuya/tuyapi). Field-level confidence is marked per block; the DP table and LAN framing are well corroborated in the community, but the exact DP set on any given clone is not guaranteed — protocol version (3.3 vs 3.4), module (WB2S/CB2S/WB3S) and DP layout vary per productId and must be discovered per unit (see tuya_lan_protocol.discovery and the notes on the DPS table).

variants.notes: Canonical representative with a public teardown (Tuya Expo product 602455; ESPHome device page). WB2S module (Beken BK7231T) + RunJet RJM8L151F6P6 sensor MCU, TuyaMCU UART at 9600 8N1. Gas-only DP set (DPs 1,2,3,5,8,9,10,12,14 documented); gas_sensor_value is a 0–100 scale ≈ percent of the fixed 7±3 %LEL trip point, not ppm.
Re-spun RQ400A on a CB2S module (Beken BK7231N). DP set presumed identical to DY-RQ400A; not independently verified.

Combustible-gas + CO combo unit, protocol version 3.4 (session-key handshake required), category rqbj. Adds the CO DPs (6, 20) and reports gas_sensor_value in ppm (scale 1) rather than the RQ400A's 0–100 trip-percent scale. DP model from the tuya-local cloud dump (issue #2434).

entities.name: Gas Alarm
entities.notes: The safety entity. 0/alarm = leak detected (latched by the MCU until the level falls below half the fixed trip point), 1/normal = OK. Also pushed live via STATUS/UPDATEDPS — subscribe, don't just poll.

entities.name: Gas Level
entities.notes: Scale is variant-dependent: DY-RQ400A reports 0–100 ≈ percent of the 7±3 %LEL trip point (treat as a relative level, unitless); the C2 combo reports ppm. Confirm against the unit before attaching a unit.

entities.name: Audible Alarm
entities.notes: SAFETY: turning this off disables the buzzer — the primary local alert. Surface accordingly.

entities.name: Muffle Alarm
entities.notes: Silences the active alarm once; DP 14 auto-resets.

entities.name: Alarm Melody
entities.notes: RQ400A: five melodies (0–4); the labels are ordinal placeholders — the firmware does not name them.

entities.name: Sensor Preheat
entities.notes: True while the sensor element warms up; readings invalid meanwhile.

local_access.notes: The Tuya LAN protocol (UDP 6666/6667 discovery, TCP 6668 control) is native local access once the local key is known — no bridge hardware required. Home Assistant paths: localtuya (HACS) or make-all/tuya-local, which ships ready-made configs for this family (rq400a_gasalarm, digma_disenseg1_gassensor, boundless_pa210w_gasalarm). Firmware replacement (LibreTiny/ESPHome, OpenBeken) is the no-Tuya-at-all path and additionally survives Tuya cloud death with zero local-key step.

table.description: Result of the most recent MCU self-test.
THE safety datapoint: combustible-gas alarm status. Latched by the MCU at the fixed 7±3 %LEL trip point until the level falls below half of trip; not clearable over Wi-Fi.
Gas level reading. Scale is variant-dependent: on the DY-RQ400A a 0–100 scale ≈ percent of the trip point; on the C2 combo, ppm (scale 1). Check the unit before interpreting.
CO alarm status (combo units only, e.g. C2).
Trigger an MCU self-test; result lands in DP 1.
Sensor warm-up in progress (readings invalid while true).
Enable/disable the audible buzzer. SAFETY: disabling removes the primary local alert — surface this prominently in any UI.
Silence the currently active alarm once; auto-resets.
CO reading (combo units only, e.g. C2).

tuya_lan_protocol.authentication: per-device 16-char local key (issued at pairing; AES key)

commands.0x07: CONTROL — set one or more DPs: {"dps": {"<dp>": <value>}}
commands.0x08: STATUS — DP state report/push from the device
commands.0x09: HEART_BEAT — keep-alive (device answers with the same command)

tuya_lan_protocol.data_model: State is a DPS (datapoint) map, pushed and queried as JSON {"dps": {"1": ..., "2": ...}} keyed by numeric DP id as a string. The DP semantics for the rqbj family are in the `dps` table below. DP ids and even their meaning vary per productId — always cross-check a new unit with a DP dump (tinytuya scan) before trusting the table.

discovery.response: Datagrams carry the device id (stable identity), product key (match against device.variants) and protocol version ("3.1"/"3.3"/"3.4") — the version determines which command set and crypto path to use.

encryption.key: the per-device local key (16 chars, used directly as the AES-128 key)
encryption.notes: Protocol 3.1/3.3 encrypt the payload with the local key directly. Protocol 3.4 (e.g. the C2 combo variant) prepends a session-key handshake (commands 0x03/0x04/0x05) that negotiates a per-session key derived from the local key plus exchanged nonces — see tinytuya for the exact exchange. The discovery broadcast payload on 3.3/3.4 is encrypted with a well-known SDK-embedded key documented in tinytuya/tuyapi (not reproduced here).

framing.layout: Every message: 4-byte header 0x000055aa, 4-byte sequence number, 4-byte command, 4-byte payload length, payload, 4-byte integrity, 4-byte trailer 0x0000aa55. On 3.1 the integrity field is CRC32 of everything from sequence through payload; 3.3 messages additionally prefix the encrypted payload with a 12-byte version marker ("3.3" + padding) and 3.3/3.4 replace the CRC32 with HMAC-SHA256 truncated to 32 bytes. Same framing on TCP 6668 and the UDP discovery datagrams.

tuyamcu_uart.role: The sensor MCU owns the gas element, buzzer, LEDs and the 433MHz receiver; the Wi-Fi module polls/reports DPs and relays configuration. Gas detection and the local alarm work with the Wi-Fi side dead.
